papers_read.title_as_printed: Cortical and subcortical gray matter abnormalities in mild cognitive impairment (Wang et al., Neuroscience 557 (2024) 81-88)
Machine learning approaches to mild cognitive impairment detection based on structural MRI data and morphometric features (Zubrikhina et al., Cognitive Systems Research 78 (2023) 87-95)

what_each_reports.P-50: Linear SVM on combined VBM subcortical volume/shape + SBM sulcal depth/gyrification features, LOOCV, 24 MCI vs 22 NC from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital neurology clinic: accuracy 0.89, sensitivity 0.87, specificity 0.90, AUC 0.89 (subcortical-only 0.78, SBM-only 0.84 accuracy). No confidence interval.
what_each_reports.P-99: FreeSurfer 906-feature morphometry, chi-squared SelectKBest, best model RBF SVC, 10-fold CV, 145 MCI vs 62 HC from a Moscow memory clinic: accuracy 0.73 +- 0.059, ROC-AUC 0.735 +- 0.076, F1-macro 0.683 +- 0.063 (Table 1).

quantity_a: Cross-validated (LOOCV) accuracy/AUC of a linear SVM on hand-selected group-difference morphometric features for MCI vs NC in a 46-person single-centre Chinese clinic sample (MCI defined by MMSE 25-26, MoCA 19-25, memory complaint), 3T Philips.
quantity_b: 10-fold CV accuracy/AUC of an RBF SVC on automatically selected FreeSurfer features for MCI (ICD-10 F06.7, age >65) vs HC in a 207-person Moscow memory-clinic sample, 1.5T Toshiba, imbalanced classes.
incompatible_if_same: Possibly, if one pooled population and one feature set were at issue: P-50 AUC 0.89 lies outside P-99's AUC 0.735 +- 0.076 (fold SD). But neither paper claims a result about the other's cohort or features, and neither states an ordering (VBM+SBM beats FreeSurfer) that the other refutes.

gates.task: match: both MCI vs normal-control detection from baseline structural MRI (T1).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: P-50 is a local Nanjing clinic cohort, P-99 a local Moscow clinic cohort; neither uses ADNI or any shared dataset. No waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: match in substance: both internal cross-validation only (LOOCV vs 10-fold); registry V1 vs V2 differ only by CV scheme.

endpoint_and_metric: compatible metric type (accuracy and ROC-AUC both reported), but the population behind the label 'MCI' differs (P-50 clinic MCI with MMSE 25-26 and memory complaint; P-99 ICD-10 F06.7 memory-clinic patients over 65) and the predictor set differs (group-difference-selected VBM/SBM regional metrics vs 906 FreeSurfer features).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-50's 0.89 accuracy is below the 0.97 threshold (though N=46 with LOOCV and features selected from group differences in the same sample, which the paper itself lists as a limitation); P-99 is 0.73.
independence: Distinct studies: different authors, sites, countries and cohorts. No shared data.
grounds: The dataset-family gate fails with no waiver: P-50 recruited 46 participants from a Nanjing neurology clinic, P-99 207 participants from a Moscow memory clinic.
The population behind the MCI label differs: P-50 used MMSE 25-26 and MoCA 19-25 criteria, P-99 used ICD-10 F06.7 diagnoses in patients over 65.

The predictor set and input representation differ (VBM/vertex/SBM metrics selected from group-difference regions vs 906 FreeSurfer features with chi-squared selection), the same representation confound that reclassified precedent C-80.
Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes; each reports one classifier's CV score on its own cohort.

evidence_quotes.quote: The present study included 24 MCI individuals and 22 normal controls (NCs). All participants were recruited from neurology clinic of Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital.
SVM achieved the best performance when incorporating all cortical and subcortical features with an accuracy of 89 %, sensitivity of 87 %, specificity of 90 %, and AUC of 0.89
leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) was selected to evaluate the performance of the classification model
First, the sample size of the study was relatively small, and more subjects should be recruited in the future study to draw more accurate conclusions.
The dataset for the study consists of 62 healthy volunteers and 145 patients with MCI obtained from the «Memory Clinic» (Moscow, Russia).
Patients over the age of 65 who had been diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (F06.7) were eligible.
the best and most stable results were obtained by SVC (0.68 F1, 0.735 ROC -AUC)

record_defects: claim_a says 'N=46 ADNI subset': P-50's 46 participants were recruited from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital, not ADNI.
resolution_note attributes the gap to 'ADNI-specificity'; neither paper uses ADNI.
claim_a labels the method 'VBM + SBM'; the 89% model also includes FIRST vertex-based subcortical shape features.

The long list of 'bridging evidence' papers are other studies' headline scores; none is shown to identify a condition separating these two results, so the partially_resolved status is not supported by them.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only a shared cohort or a shared feature set evaluated in both populations (e.g., P-50's pipeline applied to P-99's Moscow cohort yielding a significantly different score) would make these the same quantity; nothing in either paper provides that.
